svg.title: One function app, three triggers, three failure behaviours
svg.desc: The function app func-cedar-ops-dev contains three functions. Scheduled: HealthSchedule has a timer trigger with a six-field NCRONTAB expression read from the app setting HealthSchedule, 0 0 3 * * 1-5, which is 03:00 UTC or 06:00 in Amman on Monday to Friday; it does no work itself and writes one message to the storage queue ops-health-requests through a queue output binding. Event-driven: HealthCheck has a queue trigger on that queue; it reads Dataverse, logs one line and creates at most one task; the release pipeline and a person can put messages into the same queue. Event-driven: CspReport has an HTTP trigger, POST api/csp-report, anonymous; browsers post policy violation reports; it parses, bounds, scrubs and logs. Below, a table of what happens when a function fails: the timer is not retried and runs again at the next occurrence, only one instance fires across scaled-out instances, and IsPastDue tells that an occurrence was missed; the queue message becomes visible again after the visibility timeout and is retried until the dequeue count reaches the maximum, here 3, then it is moved to the queue ops-health-requests-poison; the HTTP caller gets a 500 and decides itself whether to retry, and a response must come within 230 seconds. A side panel shows the host and worker: the Functions host listens to triggers and the isolated worker process is your .NET application.
svg.text: func-cedar-ops-dev: a schedule asks, a queue works, an HTTP endpoint listens
a person with the queue role
When a function fails: three triggers, three behaviours
Not retried. The function runs again at the next occurrence.
One instance fires even when the app is scaled out (a storage lock).
IsPastDue = an occurrence was missed. So: let the timer only ask.
The message becomes visible again and is retried: here up to 3 dequeues,
30 seconds apart. Then it moves to ops-health-requests-poison,
where a person can read it. Nothing is lost silently.
The caller gets the error and decides. A response must arrive within
230 seconds, whatever the function timeout. A browser sending a report
never retries: the receiver must be cheap and must not fail on bad input.
